summary: AquaViva transforms NASA Earth observation data, weather forecasts, and local sensor measurements into actionable agricultural intelligence. The platform helps farmers make better decisions on crop selection, planting schedules, and flood risk management through simple, explainable recommendations powered by AI. By combining satellite-scale monitoring with on-the-ground validation, AquaViva delivers reliable insights that improve resilience, reduce losses, and support sustainable food production. Designed with accessibility and scalability in mind, the solution can be adapted to agricultural regions worldwide, enabling farmers everywhere to benefit from advanced Earth science data and climate-informed decision-making.
details:
AquaViva is a free, public decision-support web app that helps farmers in Mao and Valverde, Dominican Republic, decide what to plant next, when, and why, based on the state of water and soil in each field. It combines six NASA Earth observation sources (OPERA DSWx-S1 radar water detection, GPM IMERG rainfall, SMAP and NASA POWER soil moisture, NASADEM terrain and HLS NDVI crop vigor) with NOAA GFS/GEFS rain forecasts and readings from our own field sensor (ESP-01, ultrasonic water level, DHT11). A transparent rules engine compares at least three crop rotation strategies, including the farmer’s current one, and adds a 52-week planting calendar, zones where planting is not advised because of recurrent flooding, an estimated flood probability, a flood preparation plan and farmer photo reports. Gota, our AI analyst powered by Google Gemini, explains the results in plain language and always cites the source and date of each value.

Our creative approach is to use NASA radar water detection as the trigger for rotation decisions, cross-checked in real time by a field sensor, so each source covers what the other cannot see. We built it with PHP, Supabase, Tailwind, Alpine.js, Leaflet, Chart.js, Python, GitHub Actions and Vercel, with code written using Claude Code under our team’s review. We prioritized scientific honesty: every value shows its source, date and type, the app states its limits (for example, radar misses water bodies under about 3 ha), the example fields are labeled, and the rules still need validation by local agronomists. AquaViva supports decisions; it does not replace soil laboratory analysis, agronomists or official warnings.
